title: By Nearly Every Metric, the U.S. Is Losing the Iran War
gist: Seven months in, the U.S. war on Iran has cost an estimated $38.1 billion, pushed Brent from about $72 to $104, and failed on nearly every stated goal: Iran's proxies (notably the Houthis at Bab el-Mandeb) are ascendant, missile production has resumed underground, the regime has hardened, a ~440 kg HEU stockpile is unaccounted for, and the war has become a convoy-managed fight over Hormuz flows running at about a fifth of prewar levels.

insights.claim: Brent crude was around $104 a barrel on Sept. 17, 2026, up from roughly $72 just before the war began in February.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A ~$30 war premium is embedded in oil; de-escalation would be sharply bearish crude, escalation keeps it elevated.
insights.locator: The price of Brent crude—the global benchmark

insights.claim: Oil flows through Hormuz rose from 4-5 million barrels per day in early August to approaching 10 million under U.S. naval convoy escort, yet traffic is still roughly a fifth of prewar levels, according to Eurasia Group's Gregory Brew.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Convoy system delays a general energy crisis but doesn't remove risk; supply remains highly fragile.
insights.locator: While around 4 million to 5 million barrels

insights.claim: The U.S. naval blockade has brought Iranian oil exports to a halt.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Iranian barrels are off the market, removing a supply source that had flowed largely to China.
insights.locator: While around 4 million to 5 million barrels

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 750-mile East-West pipeline to Yanbu after a drone attack blamed on Iran-backed Iraqi militants, affecting roughly 4 percent of world oil supply with no clear restart date.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Loss of the Hormuz bypass tightens supply further; watch restart timing as a key oil catalyst.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia also temporarily shut down

insights.claim: Iran has now proved it can shut down the Strait of Hormuz long term, a capability it long claimed but had never demonstrated.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Markets must permanently price a credible Hormuz closure risk even after the war ends.
insights.locator: But for all of those costs

insights.claim: The Houthis seized Mocha and strategic islands including Perim in September 2026, gaining effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the ability to act on threats to close it.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A second chokepoint at risk compounds shipping disruption and freight-rate upside.
insights.locator: Tehran’s proxies also remain a major threat

insights.claim: Houthi-Saudi exchanges of fire have revived the Yemen war paused by the 2022 truce, raising fears of a return to full-blown civil war.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Direct Saudi exposure to Houthi strikes adds risk to Saudi energy infrastructure.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the Houthis and Saudi Arabia

insights.claim: Hamas and Hezbollah are far weaker than a few years ago, but almost entirely due to Israeli actions in Gaza and Lebanon rather than the U.S. war.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: U.S. operations haven't reduced proxy threats; Red Sea/Iraq proxies are now the main risk vector.

insights.claim: Despite Hegseth's April claim that Iran could 'no longer build missiles,' intelligence reports indicate Iran has resumed ballistic missile production in underground facilities, and cheap drones remain hard to eliminate.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Iran's strike capacity persists, so Gulf infrastructure attacks remain a live risk.

insights.claim: Although Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other leaders were killed, the Iranian regime has calcified, now dominated by pragmatic but uniformly anti-Western military-security leadership.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A harder-line Tehran reduces odds of a quick negotiated settlement.
insights.quote: Insofar as regime change was a goal, U.S. action has been almost entirely counterproductive.
insights.locator: Though top Iranian leaders, including former

insights.claim: The war has cost the U.S. an estimated $38.1 billion so far, is highly unpopular, and a growing number of congressional Republicans are voting to end it, with one GOP congressman moving to impeach Hegseth.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Rising domestic political pressure increases odds of U.S. de-escalation, a major oil-price downside catalyst.
insights.locator: The United States has had military successes

insights.claim: Iran retains a roughly 440-kilogram stockpile of highly enriched uranium of unknown location, and the IAEA has conducted no in-field verification in Iran for more than six months.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Unverified HEU keeps nuclear-breakout tail risk alive and gives the U.S. a pretext for renewed strikes.
insights.quote: We have not conducted any in-field verification activities in Iran for more than six months

insights.claim: CSIS satellite analysis shows a surge in 2026 construction at Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected nuclear site, and Trump warned Iran 'not to get cute' or be hit very hard.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
entities: Center for Strategic and International Studies
insights.so_what: Pickaxe Mountain is a potential escalation trigger to monitor.

insights.claim: The administration has shifted toward economic strangulation via a naval blockade and Treasury's 'Operation Economic Outcast' sanctions campaign, though Iran has withstood U.S. economic pressure for decades.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Expect expanded secondary sanctions risk for entities dealing with Iran; unlikely to force quick concessions.
insights.locator: The administration has moved to strangle

insights.claim: A White House official said Trump has 'no need to negotiate' and is satisfied letting 'the inevitable Iranian collapse play out,' while there is little evidence Tehran is eager for a deal.
insights.speaker: John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: No near-term negotiated end looks likely; position for a prolonged conflict and sustained oil premium.
insights.quote: The President is satisfied letting the inevitable Iranian collapse play out
